subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Third-Wave Cafés: Blue Bottle to Intelligentsia
description: A micro-lesson that makes Third-Wave Cafés: Blue Bottle to Intelligentsia usable.

hook.text: In the early 2000s, a new breed of cafés emerged—treating coffee like artisan wine, not a commodity drink.

buildup.text: Blue Bottle, Intelligentsia, Stumptown, and Counter Culture led the movement with single-origin beans and precise brewing.

discovery.text: These shops sourced directly from farmers, roasted in small batches, and trained baristas like professional sommeliers.

twist.text: A pour-over at a third-wave café takes 4 minutes and costs $6–8. The patience required feels radical in a fast-food nation.

climax.text: Third-wave cafés proved that coffee quality had a ceiling only when care stopped. They raised the bar for everyone.

punchline.text: Slower, costlier, intentional. Craft coffee rewrote the American café.

quiz.question: What defines third-wave coffee culture?
options: Treating coffee like artisan wine with single-origin sourcing and precise brewing

details.summary: Third-wave cafes like Blue Bottle, Intelligentsia, and Counter Culture treat coffee as a craft product with distinct origin, processing, and roast characteristics. They emphasize direct sourcing, precise brewing, and barista skill.
details.whyItMatters: Third-wave cafes created the market for specialty coffee and demonstrated that consumers will pay premium prices for transparency, quality, and craft.
takeaways: Blue Bottle, Intelligentsia, and Counter Culture led the third wave
They treat coffee as a craft product, not a commodity
Direct sourcing and precise brewing define the movement

faq.question: What makes a cafe third wave versus second wave?
faq.answer: Third wave cafes prioritize single-origin beans, light roasting, manual brew methods, and barista expertise. Second wave cafes like Starbucks use blends, darker roasts, and automated machines focused on consistency. Third wave treats each coffee as unique; second wave aims for uniform experience.

faq.question: Are third wave cafes becoming mainstream?
faq.answer: Yes. Many third-wave principles like single-origin labeling, lighter roasts, and pour-over options have been adopted by larger chains. Blue Bottle was acquired by Nestle. The line between waves is blurring as specialty coffee practices spread to a broader market.
